title: Read a tiny CSV table
summary: CSV stores table rows as text, often with commas between fields. A CSV reader handles fields more carefully than splitting every line yourself.
introduction: CSV stores table rows as text, often with commas between fields. A CSV reader handles fields more carefully than splitting every line yourself. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain read a tiny csv table
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: CSV stores table rows as text, often with commas between fields. A CSV reader handles fields more carefully than splitting every line yourself.

blocks.code:
import csv
from io import StringIO
text = "type,count\nstory,4\nscience,2\n"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(StringIO(text)))
print(rows[0]["count"])
blocks.title: Read a tiny CSV table

blocks.text: The output displays 4, but its value is text. DictReader uses the header names as keys. StringIO lets the reader treat the sample string like a file.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Convert the count with int and add 1.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A value read from CSV is not automatically a number.
